title: Follow the Norm: Accounting for Fine-Tuning and Prompt Effects on Model Rationales
abstract: arXiv:2608.13250v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Normative datasets are often used to train and align AI systems, but the norms they contain can function as action-guiding patterns rather than neutral moral knowledge. We propose treating the AI system as a proxy actor and test whether dataset-level norms can shift it away from its baseline safety behavior when it faces high-conflict dilemmas. We make three contributions. First, we demonstrate in controlled experiments that norm-breaking fine-tuning yields norm-divergent actions justified by self-interested rationales, suggesting a systematic shift in patterns of justification. Second, we establish a practical audit trail linking downstream justifications to upstream norms using mixed methods. Third, we show that system prompts can both suppress and elicit these patterns. We conducted experiments on three models (LLaMA-3.2-11B, Qwen-3.5-9B, and Pixtral-12B) using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) fine-tuning on Social Chemistry 101 Fairness/

translated_title: 遵循规范：考量微调与提示对模型推理的影响
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.13250v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：规范性数据集常被用于训练和对齐人工智能系统，但其中包含的规范可能作为行动指导模式而非中立道德知识发挥作用。我们提议将人工智能系统视为代理行为者，并测试当面对高冲突困境时，数据集层面的规范是否能使其偏离基线安全行为。我们做出三点贡献。首先，我们在受控实验中证明，打破规范的微调会产生偏离规范的行为，并以自利性推理为依据，表明推理模式发生系统性转变。其次，我们建立了一条实用的审计线索，通过混合方法将下游推理与上游规范联系起来。第三，我们表明系统提示既能抑制也能激发这些模式。我们在三个模型（LLaMA-3.2-11B、Qwen-3.5-9B和Pixtral-12B）上使用低秩适应（LoRA）微调，在Social Chemistry 101公平性基准上进行了实验。
tldr: 本文通过受控实验证明，打破规范的微调会使AI模型在冲突困境中产生自利性推理偏离，并建立审计线索和提示控制方法，以揭示和调节数据集规范对模型行为的影响。
en_tdlr: This paper demonstrates through controlled experiments that norm-breaking fine-tuning shifts AI models toward self-interested rationales in high-conflict dilemmas, and establishes an audit trail and prompt-based controls to reveal and regulate dataset norm effects on model behavior.
